defaults.permitted_development: In Wales there is no general right to keep a fixed temporary building indefinitely just because it is called temporary. The clearest national permitted development right is the temporary use of land for up to 28 days in a calendar year, with a 14-day limit for some specified uses, and moveable structures can only ride on that right while the temporary use lasts.

rules.height_rules: There is no standard national height allowance for temporary buildings. Height is judged by whether the structure remains a genuinely moveable temporary feature or becomes operational development needing permission.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth allowance. The key issues are duration, footprint, permanence, services and whether the structure goes beyond a genuinely temporary use.
rules.boundary_rules: Temporary use rights are time limited and do not override controls on access, highway safety, nuisance or protected land. A structure left in place beyond the temporary period is likely to need permission.
rules.roof_rules: There is no separate roof rule. A substantial or fixed roof structure is more likely to be treated as building work rather than a simple temporary use.
rules.materials_rules: Use lightweight, reversible materials that support the temporary case. Permanent-looking cladding, heavy foundations and fully serviced installation make it harder to argue that the structure is only temporary.

On exposed or visitor-facing sites, anchoring, appearance and clutter can become bigger issues than the word temporary suggests.
